newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen refraining from open market oeprations.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen refraining from open market oeprations.

text.p: The Federal Reserve Bank of New York is expected to refrain from open market operations on Tuesday, economists said.
"I think they'll probably stay out today," said Kevin Flanagan, first vice president at Dean Witter Reynolds.
"Tomorrow is the end of the (two-week) maintanence period, I wouldn't rule out them coming in and giving you an overnight system. But they're unlikely to do anything today," he added.
Analysts at consulting firm MMS International also expect the Fed to remain out of the market.
Pundits did not discount the possibility of a coupon pass on Tuesday, though some of them said the operation was unlikely given the market's current liquidity levels.
"You still have the legacy of the coupon pass ... With the new methodology this could be spread out over a few weeks. So they could come in at any time and buy coupons again," Flanagan said.
At 0910 EST/1410 GMT, the federal funds were traded at 5-3/16 percent, slightly below the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
